bluf: Authentication service violates single-responsibility and exposes timing side-channel; patch required before merge.

findings.claim: authenticate() function mixes authentication, password hashing, and session creation - violates single-responsibility principle
Timing side-channel in password comparison: standard equality check allows timing attacks for user enumeration
Add rate limiting per IP address to prevent credential stuffing attacks
findings.notes: Not a current defect but recommended defense-in-depth

findings.claim: Over-engineered: JWT claims include department and manager fields never used by current consumers
findings.notes: Remove unused fields to reduce token size and attack surface

findings.claim: Session store interface is correctly abstracted behind SessionStore interface (good DI practice)

assumptions.statement: Database connection is handled by separate connection pool module
Session tokens are validated by middleware before reaching this handler
assumptions.evidence: Not verified - would require tracing middleware chain

assumptions.statement: Password hashing uses bcrypt with cost factor 12
